chunks: Al-Bazofari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a muqatib (a slave who has contracted for his manumission) who died and left wealth, saying: 'His wealth is divided according to the portion of it that was freed for his heirs, and what was not freed is accounted for his masters who contracted with him; it is their wealth.'
The manner [of this ruling] is such that all the narrations are safe from contradiction.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful, a title referring to Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a freed slave divided if he dies before completing his manumission contract?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the estate of a deceased muqatib is divided proportionally: the portion corresponding to the paid value belongs to the heirs, while the unpaid balance remains the property of the masters. This ruling, transmitted through Ahmad ibn Idris, underscores the legal continuity of the manumission contract and ensures equitable distribution of assets between familial lineage and the former owner's financial interest. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise calculation of contractual obligations in inheritance matters.
